events.text: Utterson comes home in low spirits and studies Jekyll's will in his business room.
events.quote: he took up a candle and went into his business room

events.text: The will leaves all Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde, and Hyde inherits if Jekyll vanishes.
events.quote: all his possessions were to pass into the hands of his “friend and benefactor Edward Hyde,”

events.text: Utterson calls the will madness and now fears it is disgrace.
events.quote: “I thought it was madness,” he said

events.text: Utterson goes to Cavendish Square to consult his friend Dr. Lanyon.
events.quote: set forth in the direction of Cavendish Square

events.text: Lanyon welcomes Utterson warmly as an old school and college friend.
events.quote: he sprang up from his chair and welcomed him with both hands

events.text: Utterson asks whether he and Lanyon are Jekyll's two oldest friends.
events.quote: you and I must be the two oldest friends that Henry Jekyll has?

events.text: Lanyon says Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago.
events.quote: it is more than ten years since Henry Jekyll became too fanciful for me

events.text: Utterson asks Lanyon about Hyde, and Lanyon has never heard of him.
events.quote: Did you ever come across a protégé of his—one Hyde?

events.text: Utterson lies awake all night, haunted by Enfield's tale and the faceless figure.
events.quote: The figure in these two phases haunted the lawyer all night

events.text: Utterson resolves to hunt for Hyde, thinking 'If he be Mr. Hyde, I shall be Mr. Seek.'
events.quote: “If he be Mr. Hyde,” he had thought, “I shall be Mr. Seek.”

events.text: Utterson keeps watch by the by-street door at all hours until his patience is rewarded.
events.quote: Mr. Utterson began to haunt the door in the by-street of shops

events.text: A small plainly dressed man approaches the door with a key, and Utterson accosts him as Mr. Hyde.
events.quote: Mr. Utterson stepped out and touched him on the shoulder as he passed
